jobs.description:
About Peregrine

Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.

Our clients describe our support as "absolutely excellent" and our people as "instrumental to organization's success." Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair's Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.

We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.

As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.

People first. Ownership always.

We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.

At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.

At Peregrine Advisors, you will design and build the data layer for a federal enterprise platform. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.

This is a hybrid work arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and the commuting cadence varies by assignment. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.

Your first project

Your first project will likely have you taking responsibility for the accuracy and performance of your assigned components. Depending on the assignment, you may:

Design database schemas, and write the views, stored procedures, functions, and Structured Query Language (SQL) queries that run on them
Build and maintain data pipelines and extract, transform, and load (ETL) and extract, load, and transform (ELT) processes, including loads from Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3)

Help model data across Amazon Web Services (AWS) stores such as Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible), Amazon DynamoDB, and S3

4+ years of data engineering, database development, database engineering, software development, or comparable practical experience
Bachelor's degree
SQL skills across complex queries, views, stored procedures, and functions, together with relational design, normalization, and data modeling
Working expertise in Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible), covering schema design, stored procedures and functions, and indexing
Experience with Amazon DynamoDB, covering data modeling and Global and Local Secondary Indexes (GSIs and LSIs)
Performance and query tuning that addresses slow queries through indexing and execution-plan work
Experience making logical data modeling and database-design decisions for assigned components within an established platform architecture
ETL and ELT development and data integration across AWS data services such as Aurora, DynamoDB, and S3
Experience working within data security controls such as encryption, access management, and auditing
Experience loading data from S3 into the platform stores and connecting through Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) and Java Database Connectivity (JDBC)
Proficiency in writing, PowerPoint, and Excel

Preferred

An AWS certification at the associate level, such as Developer Associate or Solutions Architect Associate
Experience tuning queries that involve locking and deadlocks
Familiarity with supporting cloud-native applications in AWS through continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) and development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) practices
Ownership of physical design for Aurora and DynamoDB schemas and indexes, or the drive to grow into it
Experience in federal information technology or high-volume transaction environments
Familiarity with AI-assisted developer tools

Who You Are

You enjoy building with SQL and take responsibility for getting data right. You can take a database problem from design through delivery and stand behind how your work performs. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.

What You Bring

Solid SQL on a modern relational platform, Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible), with stored procedures, functions, and views that hold up in use
Practical skill in query tuning against slow queries, indexing, and execution plans, together with data loading, connectivity, version control, and clean delivery
Practical experience developing logical data models and database schemas, and making database-design decisions for assigned components within the established platform architecture
The ability to own assigned database work from design through maintenance, working within data security controls, with sound judgment where accuracy and auditability are not optional

When we talk

Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned.

Benefits

This is a full-time W-2 position with a salary of $120,000 to $140,000 per year.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance with the employee premium fully paid and half of dependent premiums; employer-paid life, accidental death, and short-term and long-term disability insurance; a 401(k) with an employer match of up to 4% of salary; unlimited paid time off; and sponsored professional certifications and continuing education.

What We Offer

You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.

What We Commit To

As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.

We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

JOB TITLE: Manufacturing Data Engineer
LOCATION: Foster City, CA (Onsite)
PAY RANGE: $68 - $78/hr.
DURATION: 12 Months

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Client is seeking a Data Engineer (Contract) to design, build, and maintain the data pipelines and models powering our Manufacturing Intelligence data lakehouse. This is an onsite contract position based at our headquarters in Foster City, CA. You'll bring manufacturing data from on-prem databases, SAP MES, SAP HANA, test and diagnostics systems, etc., into the MOPS lakehouse, and shape it into trusted tables for KPIs, dashboards, and AI use cases. About 80% of the role is hands-on data engineering. The other 20% keeps the pipelines deployable, observable, and cost-efficient: CI/CD, AWS ingestion infrastructure, and MOPS-scoped Databricks configuration. You'll also work on our migration from Redshift to Databricks, and partner closely with the Data Engineering, Data Analytics, Manufacturing Operations, and Databricks platform team.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Build batch and streaming ingestion into Delta Lake using Auto Loader, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Lakeflow Connect, or Structured Streaming, including CDC feeds from AWS DMS and SAP SLT.
Design and maintain bronze, silver, and gold (medallion) layers that follow MOPS naming conventions and data dictionary standards.
Build incremental dbt models on Databricks (dbt-databricks), using MERGE and upsert patterns, SCD Type 2, and handling for late or out-of-order records.
Model manufacturing data for analytics, such as a single source of truth per unit (SFC), work orders, nonconformances, station results, and first-pass yield, and feed the semantic layer used by analysts.
Process large and semi-structured data, such as JSON test payloads, using PySpark and Databricks SQL.
Tune pipeline performance and cost through liquid clustering or partitioning, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, file sizing, and right-sized job compute.
Own data quality with dbt tests, Lakeflow expectations, and Lakehouse Monitoring, including freshness SLAs and alerting.
Orchestrate workloads with Databricks Workflows or Airflow.
Migrate existing Redshift models and pipelines to Databricks: translate SQL, run in parallel, reconcile results, and cut over.
Partner with analysts and manufacturing stakeholders on requirements, and document lineage, data contracts, and table definitions in Unity Catalog.
Build and maintain CI/CD for MOPS jobs, pipelines and dbt models with Databricks Asset Bundles and GitHub Actions, across dev, staging and prod.
Manage MOPS-owned catalogs, schemas, volumes and grants in Unity Catalog, following the central platform team's governance model.
Configure job compute and SQL warehouses within central cluster policies; manage MOPS service principals, secret scopes, and OAuth machine-to-machine auth for Airflow and dbt.
Configure and troubleshoot the AWS ingestion layer that feeds the lakehouse (DMS, Kinesis, S3 landing buckets, IAM roles), partnering with infrastructure owners on provisioning through Terraform.
Monitor job health and DBU spend using system tables and tagging, and set up alerting for failures and SLA misses.
Document pipelines, runbooks, and operational procedures, and take part in incident response and root cause analysis for data pipeline issues.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Strong SQL and Python, including PySpark.
Hands-on production experience on Databricks: Delta Lake, Unity Catalog permissions, Workflows or jobs, and Spark performance tuning.
Production experience with dbt, including incremental models and tests.
Solid grasp of dimensional modeling, the medallion pattern, and CDC and incremental loading.
Experience deploying data code through Git-based workflows and CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions, Databricks Asset Bundles or similar).
Working knowledge of AWS data services (S3, IAM, DMS, or Kinesis) and infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate or Professional; AWS certification (e.g., Solutions Architect Associate) a plus.
Experience preparing data for Databricks AI/BI dashboards, Genie, or ML and LLM use cases.
Background in manufacturing or industrial data, such as quality, yield, traceability, or MES.
Understanding of data governance and compliance as they relate to data pipelines.

EDUCATION:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 6+ years in data engineering.

Shields Group Search is partnering with a well-funded, early-stage AI infrastructure startup building the trust and security layer for the rapidly emerging AI agent economy.
As AI agents increasingly act autonomously on behalf of individuals and businesses, from booking services and accessing APIs to executing financial transactions, companies need infrastructure that can determine which agents are legitimate, who they represent, what actions they're authorized to perform, and whether their behavior presents a security or fraud risk.
Our client is building real-time verification and decisioning infrastructure that enables businesses to safely interact with AI agents at scale.
The platform combines agent identity verification, behavioral intelligence, risk assessment, and security controls to distinguish legitimate automated activity from suspicious or malicious behavior.

We're looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer to build the models that distinguish a trusted AI agent from an attack, in real time and under load.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly technical founding-stage engineering team and take meaningful ownership of mission-critical ML infrastructure.
What You'll Be Working On
The models behind this platform operate directly on the production request path. They must evaluate activity and support trust decisions in real time, under the same strict latency constraints as the rest of the infrastructure.
There is no offline batch job to hide behind and no second chance if a prediction is too slow or incorrect.

You'll work on problems involving:

Real-Time Fraud & Threat Detection:
Develop ML models that identify potentially fraudulent, malicious, or unauthorized agent activity while minimizing false positives.
Behavioral & Anomaly Detection:
Identify suspicious patterns, anomalous agent interactions, and emerging risks across automated transactions and API activity.
Low-Latency ML Inference:
Build and optimize production model-serving systems capable of making accurate decisions under demanding latency and throughput requirements.
Cold-Start & Low-Label Learning:
Develop effective detection approaches when labeled examples are scarce, including unsupervised learning, weak supervision, and custom evaluation datasets.
End-to-End ML Ownership:
Build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve production ML systems, from data and feature pipelines through real-time serving.
Adversarial ML:
Help build systems that remain effective as malicious actors adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Agentic AI Infrastructure:
Work at the intersection of modern ML, AI agents, tool calling, identity verification, and security.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

3+ years of professional ML experience
, ideally 5+ years, building, evaluating, and deploying production models, not just research or notebooks.
Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow); solid SQL.
Production ML systems end to end: feature pipelines, training, evaluation, and low-latency, real-time serving.
Comfort with low-label and cold-start problems, including anomaly detection, unsupervised methods, weak supervision, and building evaluation sets and labels from scratch.
Data analysis, statistics, and experiment design.
Strong software engineering. You ship versioned, testable, reproducible code, not throwaway models.
Experience working in highly technical engineering environments with strong software engineering standards.
Ability to take ownership, solve ambiguous problems, and ship production-grade solutions in a fast-moving startup environment.

Strongly Preferred

Applied ML in fraud, risk, abuse, account integrity, or security.
Experience building ML models for fraud prevention, threat detection, trust and safety, or other systems designed to prevent malicious activity.
Graph ML / GNNs, sequence or behavioral modeling, or anomaly detection.
LLM / NLP work, and familiarity with AI agents, including tool use, function calling, and MCP.
Experience in adversarial settings, where the threat evolves against the model.
Explainable, auditable, reproducible ML, with real model versioning.
Experience developing ML systems at highly technical, engineering-driven companies, particularly those working on large-scale infrastructure, payments, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, or AI platforms.

Familiarity with real-time transaction monitoring, behavioral risk scoring, or identity verification systems.

Build incremental dbt models on Databricks (dbt-databricks), using MERGE and upsert patterns, SCD Type 2, and handling for late or out-of-order records.
Model manufacturing data for analytics, such as a single source of truth per unit (SFC), work orders, nonconformances, station results, and first-pass yield, and feed the semantic layer used by analysts.

Own data quality with dbt tests, Lakeflow expectations, and Lakehouse Monitoring, including freshness SLAs and alerting.
Orchestrate workloads with Databricks Workflows or Airflow.
Migrate existing Redshift models and pipelines to Databricks: translate SQL, run in parallel, reconcile results, and cut over.

Monitor job health and DBU spend using system tables and tagging, and set up alerting for failures and SLA misses.
Document pipelines, runbooks, and operational procedures, and take part in incident response and root cause analysis for data pipeline issues.

Strong SQL and Python, including PySpark.
Hands-on production experience on Databricks: Delta Lake, Unity Catalog permissions, Workflows or jobs, and Spark performance tuning.
Production experience with dbt, including incremental models and tests.
Solid grasp of dimensional modeling, the medallion pattern, and CDC and incremental loading.
Experience deploying data code through Git-based workflows and CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions, Databricks Asset Bundles or similar).
Working knowledge of AWS data services (S3, IAM, DMS, or Kinesis) and infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate or Professional; AWS certification (e.g., Solutions Architect Associate) a plus.
Experience preparing data for Databricks AI/BI dashboards, Genie, or ML and LLM use cases.
Background in manufacturing or industrial data, such as quality, yield, traceability, or MES.
Understanding of data governance and compliance as they relate to data pipelines.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 6+ years in data engineering.

Shields Group Search is partnering with a well-funded, early-stage AI infrastructure startup building the trust and security layer for the rapidly emerging AI agent economy.
As AI agents increasingly act autonomously on behalf of individuals and businesses, from booking services and accessing APIs to executing financial transactions, companies need infrastructure that can determine which agents are legitimate, who they represent, what actions they're authorized to perform, and whether their behavior presents a security or fraud risk.
Our client is building real-time verification and decisioning infrastructure that enables businesses to safely interact with AI agents at scale.
The platform combines agent identity verification, behavioral intelligence, risk assessment, and security controls to distinguish legitimate automated activity from suspicious or malicious behavior.

We're looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer to build the models that distinguish a trusted AI agent from an attack, in real time and under load.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly technical founding-stage engineering team and take meaningful ownership of mission-critical ML infrastructure.
What You'll Be Working On
The models behind this platform operate directly on the production request path. They must evaluate activity and support trust decisions in real time, under the same strict latency constraints as the rest of the infrastructure.
There is no offline batch job to hide behind and no second chance if a prediction is too slow or incorrect.

You'll work on problems involving:

Real-Time Fraud & Threat Detection:
Develop ML models that identify potentially fraudulent, malicious, or unauthorized agent activity while minimizing false positives.
Behavioral & Anomaly Detection:
Identify suspicious patterns, anomalous agent interactions, and emerging risks across automated transactions and API activity.
Low-Latency ML Inference:
Build and optimize production model-serving systems capable of making accurate decisions under demanding latency and throughput requirements.
Cold-Start & Low-Label Learning:
Develop effective detection approaches when labeled examples are scarce, including unsupervised learning, weak supervision, and custom evaluation datasets.
End-to-End ML Ownership:
Build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve production ML systems, from data and feature pipelines through real-time serving.
Adversarial ML:
Help build systems that remain effective as malicious actors adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Agentic AI Infrastructure:
Work at the intersection of modern ML, AI agents, tool calling, identity verification, and security.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

3+ years of professional ML experience
, ideally 5+ years, building, evaluating, and deploying production models, not just research or notebooks.
Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow); solid SQL.
Production ML systems end to end: feature pipelines, training, evaluation, and low-latency, real-time serving.
Comfort with low-label and cold-start problems, including anomaly detection, unsupervised methods, weak supervision, and building evaluation sets and labels from scratch.
Data analysis, statistics, and experiment design.
Strong software engineering. You ship versioned, testable, reproducible code, not throwaway models.
Experience working in highly technical engineering environments with strong software engineering standards.
Ability to take ownership, solve ambiguous problems, and ship production-grade solutions in a fast-moving startup environment.

Strongly Preferred

Applied ML in fraud, risk, abuse, account integrity, or security.
Experience building ML models for fraud prevention, threat detection, trust and safety, or other systems designed to prevent malicious activity.
Graph ML / GNNs, sequence or behavioral modeling, or anomaly detection.
LLM / NLP work, and familiarity with AI agents, including tool use, function calling, and MCP.
Experience in adversarial settings, where the threat evolves against the model.
Explainable, auditable, reproducible ML, with real model versioning.
Experience developing ML systems at highly technical, engineering-driven companies, particularly those working on large-scale infrastructure, payments, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, or AI platforms.

Payment protocols (x402), agent identity (DID / VC), or crypto commitments (Merkle anchoring).

Familiarity with real-time transaction monitoring, behavioral risk scoring, or identity verification systems.
